paper_title: How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary   Perception
caption: The QA performance, confidence, and alignment of Qwen2 under different question popularity.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The graph illustrates the relationship between question popularity and three performance metrics: Accuracy, Confidence, and Alignment, for Qwen2-7B on Songs. The x-axis, labeled "Question Popularity," has a linear scale ranging from 5 to 25, with evenly spaced numerical labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Values," also has a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 1.0, with labels at intervals of 0.2.

The graph contains three distinct lines, each representing one of the performance metrics. The blue line, representing Accuracy, starts at approximately 0.1 when Question Popularity is 5 and increases to around 0.63 when Question Popularity reaches 25, showing a continuous upward trend with a slight acceleration between 10 and 15 on the x-axis. 

The green line, representing Confidence, begins at about 0.74 when Question Popularity is 5 and rises to approximately 0.88 when Question Popularity is 25. It exhibits a gentle increase across the range, with a minor dip between 7 and 8 on the x-axis before continuing its upward trajectory.

The red line, representing Alignment, starts at roughly 0.35 when Question Popularity is 5 and climbs to around 0.78 when Question Popularity is 25. It displays a steady increase, with a more pronounced rise between 11 and 17 on the x-axis, followed by a continued but slightly slower ascent.

Overall, all three metrics demonstrate an upward trend as Question Popularity increases from 5 to 25.
model_annotations.German: This line graph illustrates the relationship between question popularity and the performance metrics of the Qwen2-7B model on songs, specifically its accuracy, confidence, and alignment. The x-axis represents question popularity, ranging from 5 to 25 in increments of approximately 3-4 units, with a linear scale. The y-axis represents the values of the three metrics, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, also with a linear scale. The graph features three lines: a blue line with circle markers representing accuracy, a green line with triangle markers representing confidence, and a red line with square markers representing alignment. The accuracy line starts at around 0.1 at a question popularity of 5, increases steadily to approximately 0.62 at a question popularity of 26. The confidence line begins at about 0.75 at a question popularity of 5, fluctuates slightly before stabilizing around 0.8 and eventually reaching 0.88 at a question popularity of 26. The alignment line commences at roughly 0.35 at a question popularity of 5, exhibits a generally upward trend, and reaches approximately 0.77 at a question popularity of 26.
